dedupe_keys.name: victoria minnesota locating a new fire station with predicted demand and a service quality index

description: This case study develops a systematic approach to choose where to build fire stations and applies it with the Victoria Fire Department in Minnesota, United States. The authors trained random forest and gradient boosting models on spatial data from several sources to predict demand for fire services, used them to define an index of fire service quality, found candidate sites with travel-time based clustering, and chose locations with a maximum coverage integer programme and a two-stage stochastic version that expresses confidence in the decision; the work is posted as a preprint, free to read online on arXiv under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is one city. Caveats: the city is small, the demand model is trained on local history, and the preprint has not been peer reviewed. The demand model achieved a true positive rate of about 80 percent and a false positive rate of about 20 percent, and the approach helped the fire department select a location for a new station, with reported gains in coverage from the new facility. Simulation uses: a template linking demand prediction to facility location for fire and emergency medical service planning. Related records: the London fire response time study (case_study-london-fire-station-closures-response-time-survival-model) analyses the opposite case of station closures.
